tip: 'Varken ... eller' is the fixed pair for neither ... nor: 'varken han eller hon'. Use 'eller' here, never 'och'.
'Kommer att' + infinitive expresses predictions, especially weather and external events.
'Istället för att' takes an infinitive: 'istället för att vänta' = instead of waiting, not instead of to wait.
'Ska' marks a planned future: 'vi ska gifta oss' = we are going to get married.
For hypotheticals Swedish uses the past tense: 'om jag var du' means if I were you, literally if I was you.
'Inte bara ... utan också' frames not only ... but also; here 'också' follows the verb: 'utan förberedde också presentationen'.
In the perfect tense an adverb like 'redan' normally sits between 'har' and the participle: 'har redan ätit'.
Present participles like 'springande' don't inflect: one form for any gender or number.
When the owner is clear from context, Swedish often uses the definite instead of a possessive: 'har förlorat passet' rather than 'sitt pass'.
The '-s' on 'ses' makes it reciprocal: 'vi ses' means we see each other, the everyday way to say see you.
When a clause like 'så länge du är här' comes first, the verb goes before the subject: 'är jag glad', not 'jag är glad'.
'Berätta' needs 'för' before the listener: 'berättade för mig' means told me. You cannot drop the 'för'.
For a length of time Swedish uses 'i': 'bott i två år' means lived for two years, not 'för'.
'Klaga' takes 'över' here for what you complain about: 'klagade över att' means complained that.
Reported speech uses past perfect ('hade fått') when the original was past tense ('fick').
Unlike English, Swedish past participles inflect like adjectives: 'en stängd dörr', 'ett stängt hus', and 'den stängda dörren'.
Present participles like 'leende' (smiling) end in '-ande' or '-ende' and keep one form no matter the noun.
'Öronbedövande' = ear-deafening: Swedish builds vivid compounds from noun + participle.
'Just' here means just now. It sits between 'har' and 'kommit' to say something happened moments ago.
The particle 'upp' reshapes the verb: 'ringa' alone means to call, and 'ringer upp' means to phone someone up, here to call back.
'Vart' means where to, for direction. 'Var' means where something sits. 'Vart vinden blåser' asks which way.
'Säga åt någon att' means tell someone to do something. The 'åt' is required: 'sa åt mig att vänta'.
When a reported question's question word is its subject, add 'som': 'vem som hade ringt', never 'vem hade ringt'.
Swedish says 'ha rätt', literally have right, to mean be correct: 'han hade rätt', he was right.
'Anställd' (employed) works as both a participle and a noun: 'de anställda' = the employees.
Start with a phrase like 'enligt honom' and the verb comes next, before the subject: 'var det', not 'det var'.
'Under all kritik' literally means below all criticism: something so bad it is beyond critiquing at all.
After 'uppmanade', put the object 'oss' first, then 'att lämna'. Pattern: urge someone 'att' plus the verb.
Swedish can drop the noun after 'den' plus adjective: here 'den blå' means the blue one, with no noun needed.
'Det sägs att' = it is said that – reporting hearsay without naming who says it.
